items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Sid and I were real tight

ctx.x: Okay. Well, see, when Joe Glaser first got that group together, the All Stars, see they called me first before Sid Catlett but I was busy then with my own little group and doing record dates and things around and I just didn't want that gig then to go out on the road. Then I didn't know how the quintet was going to go. And so they got Sid Catlett and the next thing I heard, oh goodness, after the group was about one week old, well

they were a sensation. Sid Catlett, Jack Teagarden, Earl Hines, Barney Bigard, and Louie, they were sensational. And Sid, the group, Velma Middleton singing, and that group just worked and worked and worked until Sid was-took ill, sick, then they couldn't go on the road any more. Sid and I were real tight and when they called me again for the gig I wasn't sure whether Sid was sick or not, but I had Sid's number, I called Sid at his home, they were in New York. I said "Joe Glaser has been calling me and wants me…

on records. So when I went in the drums were sitting right up front, and Barney and Jack were standing right next to me and so we're about to open and Louie, "Hey, Cozy how you doing?" All right, Louie you know, and I figured that some time during that time he'd say well, Cozy, we're going to do this, we're going to play this, we're going to play this." So I asked Barney, I said "Barney, what are we playing?" I said, "Louie hasn't said anything to me," and Barney said, "Man, don't pay Louie any mind, because…
